newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Female students file complaint against riot police.
newsitem.headline: Female students file complaint against riot police.

text.p: Seven South Korean female students filed a complaint against riot police on Thursday for alleged sexual and verbal harassment during violent pro-North Korean campus protest in August.
"The riot police verbally assaulted and grabbed the breasts of female students as they quelled the protest in a teaching block at Yonsei University on August 20," the students said in a statement.
"We filed the complaint to help prevent sexual abuse by law enforcment officers and restore respect for human rights," the statement said.

The complaint was filed with the Seoul prosecutor's office against Park In-yong, head of the National Police Administration, officers in charge of the raid and police officers who raided the teaching block.

Amnesty International earlier this month accused South Korean police of sexually assaulting female students who had been arrested as part of widespread human rights abuses after riot police stormed Yonsei.
"Female students said that the police had grabbed their breasts and other parts of their bodies and shouted sexual insults," said the London-based human rights group in a report.
Until now, 225 students have been sentenced in connection with the demonstrations at Yonsei, in which one riot policeman was killed and hundreds of other officers and students injured.
A total of 444 students have been sent to trial.

Riot police stormed Yonsei to end a seven-day occupation of two teaching blocks by militant students taking part in an annual pro-Korean unification rally and demanding the withdrawal of 37,000 U.S. troops stationed in South Korea.
The two Koreas technically remain at war since the 1950-53 Korean War ended without a peace agreement.
